Do you guys know any good tactics to control the deer? I already have a 4 ft high chicken wire fence surrounding my garden, but it sags in some areas, I did buy some bigger stakes (5 ft) to surround my garden with so that I can attach wire to the tops of them and hopefully that'll deter the deer further. I have a 6 foot fence topped at 10 feet with fishing wire around my vegetable garden. The deer are capable of jumping it, but it's enough to deter them. Also, the outside of the fence is surrounded by Bee Balm.

Some general rules I follow:

1) If the deer love it, it is not in my garden. I have removed many beautiful plants, e.g. 2 rose bushes, because the deer loved them. Why keep something in your yard that attracts them?

2) Block any deer trails. There was a deer trail through my yard that I placed a large stack (15' long x 6 1/2' high) of wood across. The deer could jump it but don't. They get nervous when they can't see what's on the other side.

3) Plant what the deer don't like. Nothing is 'deer proof'. If they're hungry enough they'll eat anything. That said they tend not to like thing with strong odor or taste, e.g. most herbs. Things like Bee Balm (mint family), Echinacea (Cone Flower), and Cat Mint work for me. Your local agriculture office can give you good local advice. I live in New Jersey and have found the Rutger List of Landscape Plants Rated by Deer Resistance to be very good.

4) What works for your neighbor may or may not work for you. I have a lot of Irises which the deer never bother. The deer consume irises at a friend's house about a mile away. So experiment. Plant more of what works and less of what doesn't. Indeed, remove what doesn't.

Good luck.

After suggestions from my neighbors, I've tried something that works really well. Take a twine and suspend it about 3-4' off the ground all the way around your garden. Now, get some old video tapes and break them open. Cut the tape into sections about 3' long. Tie every 2-3' alone the twine so that the video tape is dangling just above the ground. It works remarkably well. I'm in fruit country and our local apple/cherry farmers use mylar strips tied to the tree's to keep the deer away. IF the commercial farmers are doing it, it works!

Hang a bar of soap around your garden. Deer have an amazing sense of smell, and anything that foreign means danger to them.

Bar soap was mentioned, but It is more than that. The best to use is Irish Spring. The reason is that it smells absolutely nothing like anything in nature can make. It comes across as entirely foreign to any animal. That sort of smell is a big alert to a deer. We used to shave the soap all around the area, and replace it once a month. You don't need much the smell travels. We never had issues with deer with that.
